category_summaries.summary: The Board recognizes the Orange County Classroom Teachers Association, Inc. as the exclusive bargaining agent for all certified non-administrative personnel, and agrees to negotiate with the Association’s designated representative under Fla. Stat. ch. 447; the Association, in turn, recognizes the School Board as the duly elected representative of Orange County’s people and agrees to negotiate with the Chief Executive Officer (or his representative) under the same statute. The bargaining-unit job title definitions are subject to PERC clarification for job titles and newly created titles. The Association’s representatives are limited to no more than six (6) designees per day and three (3) designees per work location at any one time unless the principal approves otherwise; if a PERC-sanctioned representation challenge occurs, the challenger receives no greater rights than the Association. Upon request, the Board must provide the Association with a work-location listing of all teachers new to the system. For dues/uniform assessments, teachers who authorize deductions in writing (with personally signed authorization forms) have dues deduction begin with the first full pay period after the Board receives the form; the Board deducts 1/20 of the appropriate annual dues from regular paychecks after enrollment, with no deductions made in any pay period where net earnings after other deductions would be less than the dues amount. Authorization continues annually unless revoked; a teacher may revoke with 30 days’ written notice to the Board and Association, but cancellation only occurs after submission of the required standardized cancellation form to Payroll, available from either the Association or Payroll. Changes in the dues amount must be certified to the payroll administrator no later than 20 days before the effective date, and dues collected via payroll deduction are transmitted to the Association by the method specified in the agreement. The Association may select the majority of bargaining-unit members of the Teacher Education Center Council, and an additional bargaining unit may be added as needed with approval of the Director of Exceptional Education.

This Contract expires at the end of a calendar year, during which the parties will exchange successor-contract proposals by March 15 and begin negotiations by April 1 (or another mutually agreed date), with the final negotiated successor contract reduced to writing and signed by the Board and the Association. If any contract provision or application is held contrary to law, the affected provision/application is not valid to the extent permitted by law, and the parties must either immediately meet to reopen negotiations on the matter or mutually agree to address it in subsequent negotiations. Certain guidance counselors, media specialists, and other teachers are to be notified by May 1 of available five-day contract extensions for the period following post-planning, and by the end of post-planning for the period preceding pre-planning. The athletic director will be offered an extended contract of up to four weeks, with the timing of the four-week extension mutually arranged by the work site supervisor and the athletic director.

Management provisions address teacher and principal control of student discipline and classroom order (teachers maintain order and accept assigned authority; the principal/designee decides when students return and advises the teacher of the referral disposition), staffing and assignment responsibilities (instructional personnel are assigned by the Superintendent/designee based on preparation/certification/experience/aptitude; the principal determines staffing needs and where reductions occur by defined department/area, with the Superintendent able to waive requirements in unusual circumstances), and limits on certain duties (teachers are not required to accept IMPACT/duty assignments for middle school P.E. or teachers teaching six elective courses; teachers have freedom to implement adopted curriculum with the principal/supervisor’s right to question/consult/direct; teachers determine grades/promotions subject to consultation and administrator initialing on the permanent record; teachers are not required/permitted to discipline other teachers; no peer teacher may perform Beginning Teacher Program Summative Evaluations, which are solely the beginning teacher principal/immediate supervisor’s responsibility). Employment and equity protections include: supplements are not a required condition of employment; family members cannot be assigned in direct line supervision without Superintendent approval; peer teacher participation is voluntary unless no qualified volunteers, in which case assignments are sought broadly and rotated equitably; substitute use restrictions for full-time teachers generally apply only in emergencies/unforeseen circumstances for art/music/P.E. and media specialists; a teacher must have at least 16 student contact days before any formal observation; and the deputy superintendent for instruction/designee has sole prerogative for adjusting class size for an individual teacher. Additional management/organizational duties and related limitations include equitable use of special duty supplements primarily for before/after-school supervision (with Superintendent written approval for dissimilar use, equity efforts in assignment, and limits of no more than two special units per individual), department chair coordination and appointment input where a vacancy exists (supplements paid only where a department has three or more teachers including the chair), athletic staffing and coordination requirements (including certified athletic director and trainer roles, duty/qualification conditions, and release limitations), and that sabbatical leave totals are solely within the Board’s discretion.

Teachers’ salaries are set by Appendix A (regular salary) and supplemental activities by Appendices B and J, with all salary/supplement increases effective beginning July 1, 1987. Pay is calculated by dividing a teacher’s annual salary by the duty days in the teacher’s primary contract; daily-rate workshop pay (when paid in addition to annual salary) is paid using the daily rate for ten‑month teachers, and supplements are excluded from daily-rate calculations. Summer session pay is at the daily rate in effect during the immediately preceding contractual period, with summer variations to the five-day work week governed by Appendix I; supplemental salary is not included in the summer daily-rate calculation. Paychecks are issued semi-monthly in equal installments—ten‑month teachers on the 8th and 22nd, and 11/12‑month teachers on the 15th and last day—except when the payday is not a duty day (then the check is issued on the last duty day prior). Ten‑month teachers may elect deferred pay (by the last day of pre-planning): they receive 2/24 of regular salary each semi-monthly installment for ten months and the remainder in one check on June 8; post-planning salary due is paid within three working days (and within two working days if the Board selects a four-day workweek for summer). Direct deposit is available upon request, including supplemental pay. Summer employees are paid on the 8th and 22nd (first check July 8), with normal six-week summer program final salary by August 8, and supplements are distributed in equal monthly payments with timing for athletic and Band Director supplements beginning on the September 22 paycheck (if activity begins before September 1) and other known supplements beginning October 22. Additional compensation includes: mileage reimbursement (excluding home-to-base round trip) at the Florida maximum rate; toll reimbursement upon receipt; a daily room rate allowance of at least $175; terminal pay upon retirement based on daily rate × 35% × accumulated sick leave days, payable within 30 duty days (or as mutually agreed in the fiscal year), with death/beneficiary treatment provided; supplements adjusted for resignations/separations before completing supplement requirements (adjusted on the last supplemental paycheck); assistant supplement amounts set by a fraction of the head supplement (with specified exceptions); restrictions on paying multiple athletic supplements with conflicting seasons (allowing overlapping seasons up to three weeks); and irregular schedule compensation for hours between 5:30 p.m. and 7:00 a.m., weekends, or split shifts at 1.10× regular salary (not requiring over 37½ hours/week), and for regularly working 40 hours/week exclusive of meal breaks at 1.15× regular teaching salary (with similar 1.15× treatment for physical/occupational therapists). Sabbatical leave compensation is 75% of gross monthly salary based on the current salary schedule, with the contracted salary excluding supplements, summer school, or other outside-basic-contract compensation while fringe benefits continue. Teachers required to teach six periods due to legislative changes receive a $1,000 annual salary supplement. Salary-related administrative and verification adjustments provide retroactive back pay rules for experience, advanced degrees (retroactive to date of completion within the school year), and certain administrative mistakes (retroactive to the current year and up to five prior years, with limits where applicable).

Scheduling provisions require advance, equitable, and minimally disruptive handling of timetable and duty changes. Board–Association bargaining meetings mutually scheduled during the teacher duty day require relief from regular duties for members of the bargaining team, with the Board providing substitutes for up to nine teachers. Tentative teaching assignments for reappointed teachers must be noticed on or before the first day of post-planning (or immediately if acceptance occurs after that date). In emergencies, extended duty assignments beyond the regular day are permitted, with volunteers used first; if none, teachers are selected based on irre-schedulable personal commitments, and the affected teacher receives equal compensatory time during non-student contact within ten (10) duty days (or by mutual agreement). The Board will hold scheduling changes to a minimum for instructional/facility/student-request reasons and, under normal circumstances, discuss them with affected teachers prior to change. Teacher planning and break scheduling are guaranteed: daily duty-free lunch (at least 25 minutes on instruction days; one hour on non-student contact days; approximately one hour by mutual agreement where lunch facilities/flexibility do not exist, with proportionate workday extension for equity), daily assigned planning time (elementary: at least 300 minutes/week with at least 30 minutes contiguous daily), and daily breaks (22 minutes per half-day at the teacher’s discretion with supervisor approval). Teaching loads are capped and supervision rotated equitably: elementary student contact including supervision not to exceed 1,550 minutes/week (with qualifying supervision not counting toward contact time and time off provided within five duty days), and secondary student contact not to exceed 1,500 minutes/week (senior high period assignments generally limited to 1,250 of the 1,500 unless written Deputy Superintendent permission is granted for extenuating circumstances; homeroom/passing not counted except limited to 10 minutes/day or 30 minutes/week). Supervised study halls and non-compensated extracurricular/co-curricular activities during school hours are treated as teaching periods; homeroom beyond limits reduces student contact time. Principals must cooperate with morning/afternoon break arrangements (and provide the same break for teachers where students have breaks in three-hour blocks, or allow at least 10 minutes of planning time/student passing time as a duty-free break if breaks cannot be facilitated). Beginning Teacher Program required meetings/activities may not infringe guaranteed planning time or duty-free lunch, requiring relief of peer/beginning teachers of student contact time or other duties for an equivalent period. Weather/closure days are made up by extending the school year after consultation with the Association. Scheduling variations are permitted under specified conditions: irregular schedules for adult vocational teachers may be used only with notice or a meeting at least ten (10) working days before assignment (volunteer selection considering seniority/certification/experience; if none, least senior qualified teacher), with assigned duration not exceeding 45 student contact days unless mutually extended up to one school year in writing; irregular-schedule teachers receive at least two (2) weeks advance notice and information on the reasons/terms of assignment. The contract also addresses summer posting of anticipated positions for specified programs (posted no later than three weeks before the end of the second semester), and allows up to a three-day contiguous contract extension for PREP law preliminary screening for ten-month employees (with teachers reimbursed at their daily rate and notified no later than the last day of post-planning). Compressed four-day work week scheduling is Monday–Thursday (with July 4 adjustments), on-site planning periods are set for full/half days, and additional Wednesday meeting time for high school teachers may require up to 45 minutes beyond a seven-and-one-half hour day with a $300 annual supplement.

Leave provisions cover multiple leave types and administration: the Association is granted up to seventy-five (75) leave days per fiscal year for members, with a per-teacher cap of five (5) days (additional days only by Superintendent discretion), and reimbursement to the Board for non-permanent substitutes if needed; Association faculty representatives and Association Board members may leave at the end of the student day for up to three (3) regularly scheduled meetings per month. For the duly elected Association president serving as CTA president, he is released from regular duties for the term and acts as fiscal agent for his own salary/fringe benefits/fixed charges, with the Association reimbursing the Board 100% of all sums paid; during that term he earns no sick or annual leave, is not covered by Board workers’ compensation insurance, receives salary schedule credit for years served, and district-wide seniority accrues; unused sick leave may be transferred on return to Orange County at one (1) day transferred per day accrued, up to twelve (12) days per year. For long-term situations, long-term leave is administered such that replacing teachers are employed for periods tied to the length of leave, the Board notifies long-term leave persons to declare return intent by March 1, and individuals must inform the Board by February 15 and the Personnel Department by March 15; long-term leave generally ends June 30, cannot be worked full-time during the leave absent Superintendent waiver, and a failure to file intent to return is treated as a resignation effective June 30 (except extenuating circumstances). Teachers must make up lost time within ten (10) duty days after tardiness/early departure when a full 7½-hour day cannot be met, except absences requiring use of a substitute (other than the permanent substitute) are charged as leave; teachers may leave at the end of the student day for certain medical/legal/dental appointments or required school-related dependent conferences that cannot be scheduled outside duty time, with advance makeup permitted. Sick leave administration includes accrual at one day per month (credited at month-end, not usable before earned), unlimited accrual, and transfer of unused sick leave from other districts/jobs/state agencies by law (one day transferred per day accrued in Orange County, with the teacher responsible for transfer arrangements), and sick leave balances carried into approved leave with pay deductions from accumulated sick leave. A Sick Leave Bank allows eligible teachers (one school year employed and at least six (6) accrued sick days) to enroll by contributing one (1) sick day, with replenishment assessments if the Bank falls below 300 days; members may withdraw within 21 calendar days after notice or assessments are automatic otherwise, inability to contribute results in ineligibility until two (2) sick days accrue (then automatic assessment of one), and retiring teachers may donate any unused sick days. To draw from the Bank, a teacher must have a minimum of six (6) sick days at time of need, may receive up to 100 paid sick leave days per period of extended illness/accident/injury upon proper doctor support and Personnel Department approval, must use drawn days for personal illness/injury, and owes the Bank six (6) minus current accumulation with up to three (3) years to repay (deducted from final paycheck if resigning/retiring prior to repayment). Alleged Bank abuse is investigated by the Superintendent/designee and, if wrong doing is found, the member must repay all abused days subject to grievance/arbitration limited to whether the finding was justified (not split). The provisions also set related leave procedures (applications submitted to principal/supervisor on Board forms; ability to take leave in full/half-day increments; must notify changes in leave reasons; return requires a certificate of absence; Association consulted prior to modifications of forms). Additional leave categories addressed include illness/injury in-line-of-duty leave with pay up to ten (10) duty days per school year (with possible extensions for qualifying assault/battery injuries and eligibility tied to Bank/assistance criteria), personal leave with pay up to four (4) school days per year not chargeable beyond a stated rule (generally chargeable to sick leave, non-accumulable, and not available during specified periods except emergencies/limited circumstances), temporary duty leave with full pay for Board-initiated or teacher/Board-initiated temporary duty, professional leave (with pay up to ten (10) duty days over a five (5) year certificate renewal/extension cycle; and without pay up to ten (10) duty days at year beginning/end for degree-related summer school subject to not taking during student attendance), court/jury leave with pay when subpoenaed/summoned (with exceptions where the teacher is a litigant), military leave capped at 17 days per annual period for active duty/training without loss of pay/time/efficiency rating, extended military obligations leave without pay when required, and sabbatical leave for up to one (1) year after seven (7) continuous certificated years of satisfactory service (subject to additional eligibility and detailed requirements including enrollment and service obligation after leave). Annual leave for twelve (12) month employees is provided (including that it cannot be used until earned unless approved in advance, and termination triggers payment for earned annual leave within 30 duty days), with additional annual-education summer school leave provisions (up to three weeks per year cumulative to six, charged to annual leave). Finally, there is a specific termination request procedure stating the member requests termination of membership in the Sick Leave Bank.

Under the Healthcare benefits provisions, the Board provides teachers at no cost a health insurance program that is equal to or better than the current plan, including specified coverage without teacher deductible or coinsurance for items such as second/third diagnostic opinions, pre/post-admission testing, outpatient surgery, birthing center costs, certified/licensed nurse-midwives, mammography, and Hospice treatment up to $7,500; it also provides a PSC prescription plan with $5 per prescription for legend drugs and $2 per prescription for generic drugs for up to a 30-day supply, plus a mail-order 90-day option at $3 per brand-name drug and no cost for generic substitutes. Nursery care for a newborn during the mother’s hospital stay is included, and if both spouses are Board employees, their health insurance contributions are combined toward family coverage. The parties provide for voluntary plan alternatives, including an HMO plan(s) in lieu of group medical insurance as required by federal law (negotiated with the Association), and a separate voluntary alternative to the current program that replaces the current plan if chosen; teachers may re-enroll without restrictions, subject to the normal waiting period for new teachers except for unusual circumstances leaving the teacher without group health coverage. The Fringe Benefit Committee and related processes include reviewing/redeveloping insurance specifications for rebidding, discussing tiered family coverage for rebidding specifications, administering a multi-optional insurance program with $150 per teacher per year that may be applied to additional coverages (including family health, dental, optical, disability, additional life, hospital indemnity, and retirement annuities), and studying a health promotion voluntary program. For retirement, comparable health insurance is made available to individuals who have completed retirement with the retired teacher bearing premium costs; procedures allow retiring teachers to elect to forego terminal pay in exchange for an equal application of monies toward health insurance premium by April 1, 1987. Health coverage for retired substitute teachers is funded by the Board for the duration of their participation, with an annual committee review of required days to maintain benefits and written premium-adjustment notices. The Board continues basic funding for an Employee Assistance Program, provides each teacher term life insurance equal to annual salary or $7,500 (whichever is greater) paid by the Board including accidental death and dismemberment (with no extended-contract/supplement amounts), and pays benefits to the estate if no beneficiary is designated; the Association receives copies of relevant insurance policies. The Board also provides payroll deduction for long-term disability and additional life insurance, with all premium costs borne by the teacher.

Ancillary provisions include: (1) the Board will provide free payroll deductions for eligible tax-sheltered investments under IRS Code Section 403(b), the Credit Union, the U.S. Savings Bond program, specified fringe benefit insurances in the Contract, and—once feasible—the IRS Section 125 program; (2) membership in the Bank is voluntary, and voluntary withdrawal becomes effective immediately upon the Personnel Department’s receipt of written notice of intent, with no eligibility to withdraw sick leave already contributed to the Bank; and (3) the Board will purchase a retirement annuity for each teacher retiring early who is at least 58 years old and has at least 28 years of Florida Retirement System creditable service, with the annuity amount equal to the total difference in retirement income between the benefit calculated using average monthly compensation and creditable service as of the teacher’s early retirement date.

Security-related contract provisions address teacher employment continuity and assignment protections: qualified teachers (including those certified based on non-academic preparation) are entitled to the same contractual rights/privileges as teachers with equivalent certificates (E). Continuing contracts/professional service contracts of a continuing nature take effect at the start of the school fiscal year if all requirements are submitted to the Personnel Department on or before July 1, and—once issued—allow continued employment without annual reappointment (Q). The Board may issue such continuing contracts at any time when applicable, including with no additional designated waiting periods, provided prior continuing contract/professional service status and assessment in the teacher’s current standing are met; if not recommended, reasons must be provided in writing upon request (R). Teachers cannot terminate employment without first being released from their contract (S). Reappointment cannot be denied due to anticipated certificate expiration, and the Personnel Department must notify expiring-certification teachers in writing by October 1 (T). Teaching positions are generally filled with annual/continuing/professional continuing contract teachers, with limited temporary-hire exceptions (U). Teachers may not be assigned outside their certificate scope except temporarily for good cause, and involuntary transfers within the worksite may not be done to discipline a teacher (B; 4). For placements involving long-term leave and related reassignment/recall: replacement teachers are informed that employment ends with the leave term; returning teachers are initially reassigned to the original school staff structure, and new hires/assignments are restricted until displaced returnees (and specified early-return conditions) are placed (2; 1; 1–2 re long-term leave duration). If long-term leave extends beyond the equivalent of two normal school years, return placement may be in appropriate vacancies outside the original school; short returns plus additional long-term leave are treated as a combined equivalent leave (2). Involuntary worksite transfers (e.g., during reductions or staffing changes) require advance written notice (five duty days during the school year or fourteen calendar days in summer) and must follow structured voluntary/involuntary selection order, with Superintendent authority to override volunteer availability only with non-arbitrary/capricious action and discussion with the teacher and right to representation; worksite vacancy posting and timelines for determination and notice apply (2; b–c; procedures by April 15–May 6). The contract also states limits on hiring/reassignment to avoid violating reduction-in-force protections (e.g., no assignment to vacancies until transferred certified teachers are placed; no hiring in a laid-off teacher’s subject area/elementary level until eligible certified recall teachers are offered and decline/fail to accept; recall eligibility lasts three years, and salary/benefits/seniority are restored upon reemployment) and restricts duty-station changes for secondary teachers (J; N; RIF provisions; M).

Training and staff development provisions include: the Board continues to provide CPR training opportunities. Teachers have access to required district/state policy and law materials, and if a school lacks written policies/rules, the principal must advise during pre-planning and then reduce them to writing within ten (10) duty days. The Board complies with State inservice-point regulations for certificate extension and provides each teacher a record of inservice points earned at least twice each school year; teachers may seek approval for credit for training that enhances competency, including submitting written requests to Staff Development for previously unapproved training. Staff development attendance off campus is voluntary except where required for implementing a required program, and there is no mandatory staff development/inservice on the first or final day of pre-school planning or during post-school planning (except for teachers with district-wide assignments). Regarding credits, teachers volunteering to supervise a one (1) senior year intern must receive twenty (20) inservice points (to the extent permitted by State Board rules), and teachers supervising half-time junior year interns receive points based on supervision length: five (5) weeks/5 points, eight (8) weeks/8 points, or ten (10) weeks/10 points, with other weekly blocks receiving one (1) point per week (State-rule compliant); peer teachers must receive at least ten (10) inservice points for each beginning teacher (with prorating if interrupted/changed). Teachers should be notified at least thirty (30) days in advance when possible for intern supervision. For evaluation-related training timing, annual-contract teachers on duty before the close of the first nine (9) weeks must receive at least two formal observations before annual assessment, with specified observation windows (first between September 10 and the close of the first semester; second after Winter break through March 15), and the assessment must be completed no later than April 1. New-district teachers may be required to attend up to two (2) days of district-wide orientation, preceding preschool planning by no more than one (1) week, with a $50 per day stipend for required attendance.

If negotiations for collective bargaining reach an impasse, the parties must follow Florida statutory procedures and/or Public Employees Relations Commission (PERC) rules, and either party may request appointment of a mediator. The parties must not control each other’s selection of bargaining representatives and must ensure their representatives are empowered to reach tentative agreements; either party may use outside consultants at its own expense. Tentative agreements must be reduced to writing and submitted for ratification to bargaining unit members and the Board; failure to ratify makes the tentative agreements null and void, and if tentative agreements are rejected, negotiations on those matters resume. Tentative agreements reached during or after a Special Master proceeding must be submitted for ratification before the Public Hearing; any issues not ratified go to the Public Hearing. For grievances, the process generally requires initial informal discussion with the immediate supervisor within twenty (20) duty days of when the grievant knew or should have known of the incident, followed by a written grievance within six (6) duty days after the supervisor’s verbal response; failure to file within time waives the right to proceed. At any point, a party may obtain a three (3) duty day extension by written notice (unless waived) at least three (3) duty days before the relevant deadline, and deadlines may be extended by mutual agreement. If not disposed of within the step time limits, the grievant may proceed to the next step; failure to appeal within prescribed time limits waives the right to continue. Meetings and arbitration hearings occur during the teacher duty day unless the parties mutually agree otherwise. The Association may represent the grievant at any step and may present arguments and evidence; only a bargaining-unit member (or group) or the Association may file grievances. Filing a judicial or administrative proceeding to resolve a particular issue waives pursuing that issue through the grievance procedure. Grievance-related restraint/interference/coercion/discrimination/reprisal is prohibited, and grievance documents are kept in a separate grievance file rather than the official personnel file. Deadlines for Step 3/Superintendent review include a six (6) duty day appeal from Step 2 and a six (6) duty day meeting/disposition period when a meeting is requested. If the Association elects arbitration, it must notify the Superintendent within twenty (20) duty days of the Step 3 decision; arbitration uses a Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service (FMCS) panel of seven (7) arbitrators requested within ten (10) days, selected by alternate striking (or other mutually agreeable method), with FMCS-governed procedures and a binding arbitration award. Either party pays the full cost of a stenographic transcript it requests; if both mutually agree, transcript costs are split equally. During grievance meetings (other than arbitration), tape recording requires express permission of all present.

The contract requires the Board to maintain safe and healthful working conditions, provide first-aid supplies at each school, and furnish relocatable classrooms (before the first class) with standard permanent-classroom features (e.g., lighting, climate control, and necessary desks and equipment). The Board must take reasonable precautions for teacher safety and, if a teacher is harassed, threatened, suffers bodily harm, or has property loss during duty, the teacher must report in writing to the principal/supervisor (forwarded to the Superintendent), who must cooperate in any civil/criminal proceeding (including providing legal counsel) and assist with law enforcement actions; discipline for students must follow the Orange County Code of Student Conduct and action must also be taken against non-students to ensure a safe working environment. Teachers may use necessary and reasonable force to quell disturbances, protect themselves/others from injury, restrain disruptive students, or protect personal/district property; teachers may send disruptive students to the office using a principal-provided referral slip (emergencies allow immediate removal with a written report), but under no circumstances may teachers suspend students from class or school. Corporal punishment is only permitted if the principal delegates authority and the teacher consents, and only in defined circumstances; physical force used to protect against disruptive students is not treated as corporal punishment. Teachers must report contagious/infectious disease or headlice and students may not be readmitted until the principal takes appropriate action (with specified exclusion for headlice, pinkeye, and impetigo as health threats). Teachers are not required to search for bombs or be disciplined for refusing work in an unsafe/hazardous situation with imminent danger to their health/safety, except where student health and safety clearly require teacher intervention. The Board also repairs or reimburses a teacher’s personal property/clothing current value damaged or destroyed due to qualifying assaults/battery in the course of duties, unless insurance/reimbursement is otherwise obtained, capped at $200, and covers teachers under workers’ compensation insurance (with stated exclusions).

The agreements supersede any contrary Board rules, regulations, or practices, and the final Contract is issued as two signed originals (one retained by the Board and one by the Association). The parties share the cost of printing 7,200 copies of the Contract and amendments (with 6,500 provided to the Association for distribution to bargaining unit members and new teachers) to occur within 30 days after both parties ratify, unless extended by mutual agreement. Miscellaneous workplace and administrative matters include Association access and communications rights (exclusive bulletin board space of at least 9 and up to 12 square feet; use of teacher mailboxes; exclusive inter-school mail service subject to restrictions on derogatory/advocacy/campaign materials, with one flyer per candidate for Association office; and opportunities for the Association president/designee to announce non-student-hour availability by notice or intercom), Association access to meetings and announcements at faculty meetings (announcements may be made by the faculty representative or president/designee; continued attendance is voluntary; and Association faculty meetings may occur before/during/after duty day subject to exclusions for student contact time and assigned duty, capped at 1 hour per month during the duty day). The Board must provide recurring materials and policy copies (agenda packets before Board meetings, Board periodicals, and official Board policies, including revisions), provide computer printouts upon request (three sets per school year at no cost; additional sets at cost if legally releasable), grant access to non-exempt public records at mutually agreed times with staff present (copies at cost if requested), and maintain confidentiality procedures and teacher access rights for personnel/work location files and beginning teacher portfolios. Teachers and the Association also receive various logistics and governance items (e.g., Board-taught class observations only with principal permission at mutually agreeable times; each teacher may examine personnel files in the presence of a staff member; teachers may obtain copies of file documents at no cost; teachers must be encouraged/required only to notify the principal if they will not attend open house; and the Association may provide input before recommended Orange County Code of Student Conduct revisions). Additional miscellany addresses tort/legal defense and indemnity mechanics (Board compliance with Florida tort law for negligent/wrongful acts of teachers in scope of employment; Board not liable for bad faith/malicious/wanton conduct; and procedures for Board-provided legal services upon teacher request, with reimbursement if guilty or pleas occur, and public-meeting notice), patents/ownership of teacher-developed innovations (e.g., jointly owned for school-time innovations using school supplies; teacher owns non-duty-hour creations using own supplies with royalty waiver; Board owns materials created under contractual obligations; and title vests in the Board upon termination for in-school/school-supply works), restrictions on Association strike involvement with potential revocation of dues deduction privileges only for the remainder of the Contract up to the following June 30, and Board-provided custodial services for moving heavy equipment.
